scale.prompt_suffix: Would you say: not at all, a little, somewhat, mostly, or completely?

scoring_notes: Each answer is centered (answer minus 3) and multiplied by polarity, then added to every type in `loads` using that load's weight. Disambiguation items load positively on one type and negatively on its common look-alike. Instinct items load on sp/so/sx instead of types. See scoring.ts.

items.text: I notice what's wrong or out of place almost before I notice anything else.
I carry a strong inner voice that tells me how things should be done.
When I let a standard slide, it bothers me for a long time afterward.
I'm comfortable letting things be a bit sloppy if nobody cares.
I can sense what someone needs before they say it, and I move to give it.
It's much easier for me to offer help than to ask for it.
Being needed by people is a big part of how I feel good about myself.
I'm fine saying no to people even when they're disappointed in me.
I adjust how I come across depending on who I'm with, so that I succeed.
Slowing down and not being productive makes me restless or uneasy.
I care a lot about being seen as successful at what I do.
I'm fine doing work that nobody will ever see or give me credit for.
I've always felt different from the people around me, like something others have is missing in me.
My moods run deep, and I'd rather feel them fully than smooth them over.
Ordinary or generic is almost painful to me. I need things to feel authentic.
I don't spend much time wondering who I really am.
I need a lot of time alone to recharge and think things through.
I'd rather understand something completely before I act on it or speak about it.
I keep my needs small so I don't have to depend on anyone.
I'm quick to share my feelings and reactions in the moment.
My mind automatically runs through what could go wrong.
I test people and ideas before I trust them, and once I do, I'm very loyal.
I second-guess my decisions more than most people seem to.
I rarely feel the need to check with anyone before I decide.
I keep my options open, because committing to one thing feels like a trap.
When something gets painful or boring, I quickly find something more exciting.
I have far more plans and ideas than I could ever finish.
I can sit with an uncomfortable feeling without distracting myself from it.
I take charge in a group almost without deciding to.
I'd rather be respected than liked.
I have a hard time showing vulnerability, so I show strength instead.
I'm uncomfortable with confrontation and avoid it when I can.
I can see everyone's side so clearly that I lose track of my own opinion.
Keeping things calm and comfortable matters more to me than getting my way.
I tend to go along with things, and then feel quietly resentful later.
I know exactly what I want, and I say it without hesitating.
Even when I'm having fun, part of me is tracking whether it moves me toward a goal.
My carefulness comes from my own standards, more than from worry about what might happen.
I'd rather actively step in and help someone than quietly keep the peace.
When I withdraw, it's to think and save energy, not to avoid conflict.
Under stress, what I feel is more like longing and envy than fear and suspicion.
I'd rather be the one in control than the one who looks the best.
I think about money, health, comfort and safety more than most people I know.
A good day is one where my body, my space and my resources all feel taken care of.
I naturally track who's connected to whom, and where I fit in a group.
Contributing to something bigger than me, like a team or a community, is what makes work meaningful.
I'm drawn to intensity. One deep connection beats a room full of acquaintances.
I lose interest fast when there's no spark or chemistry in a situation.
